name: Redwood National and State Parks
blurb: Fog-fed giant redwoods, Roosevelt elk and the cougars and bears that follow them.

tip.title: Thin the fog
tip.text: Redwoods drink fog through their leaves and bark. Cut Coastal summer fog by 60% and watch the redwoods, then the rabbits, slugs and predators that depend on them.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Redwood National and State Parks

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Redwood National and State Parks, Sequoia sempervirens, Roosevelt elk). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Light reaches the forest floor only in patches under the tall canopy, so understory plants rely on gaps and edges.
Heavy rain on the Pacific coast feeds streams and the temperate rainforest. Fog covers much of the dry summer.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen trees, leaf litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
A conifer of the foggy coast that grows beside redwoods. Elk browse it and Douglas squirrels eat its seeds, per GloBI records.
A berry-bearing understory shrub. Elk and deer browse it, and bears and birds eat the fruit.
The large mammal most often seen in the parks. Eats grasses, ferns, shrubs and berries, and is prey for cougars and black bears.
Browses shrubs, ferns and bracken in the understory. A main prey of cougars, and its carcasses feed scavengers.
A small tree squirrel that eats conifer seeds, including those of Sitka spruce per GloBI.
A small omnivore of seeds, fruit and insects. A common prey of snakes and foxes.
A small canid that hunts mice, rabbits and shrew moles, per GloBI.
Eats rodents and frogs in GloBI records. Wikipedia notes snakes sometimes eat banana slugs.
A clever scavenger that feeds on carrion, among much else.
Finds and eats carcasses, including deer in GloBI records.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: Mostly eats plants such as berries but also hunts elk and deer calves and scavenges carrion. Fishes for salmon on the coast.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: Hunts mainly deer and elk. Bears and scavengers often take over its kills.

story: Redwood National and State Parks on the California coast protect 45 percent of the remaining old-growth coast redwood forest. The redwood is among the tallest and oldest tree species on Earth and grows in humid temperate rainforest. Chinook salmon, northern spotted owls and Steller sea lions also live here.
matters: The UN named the parks a World Heritage Site in 1980. Managers use controlled burning to restore the forest toward its condition before 1850.
